title: ‘House Of The Dragon’ Season 3 Finale: Co-Creator Ryan Condal And Star Emma D’Arcy On Rhaenyra’s Dark Path, The Battle Of Tumbleton And What’s In Store For Season 4
full_text: Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Gareth Edwards Not Returning For Next ‘Jurassic World’ Movie Bailee Madison & Deon Cole Join ‘Grown Ups 3’ At Netflix ‘X-Men’: Kit Connor Eyed For Cyclops Role In Upcoming Marvel Studios Pic View All August 9, 2026 7:10pm Emma D'Arcy in 'House of the Dragon' Courtesy of HBO SPOILER ALERT: This story contains details from Season 3 episode 8 of House of the Dragon on HBO . “I AM THE PRINCE THAT WAS PROMISED.” These are the words Queen Rhaenyra screams in the Season 3 finale to the people of King’s Landing as she unveils the future prophecy and sets the stage for what is sure to be an eventful final season. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals ‘House Of The Dragon’ Renewed For Season 4 At HBO News Ryan Condal Extends HBO Overall Deal Through Season 4 Of ‘House Of The Dragon’ & Beyond Sunday’s episode starts with the news of the return of Aegon’s dragon, leading Rhaenyra to not only put a search out for it but also have Daemon move forward with the the attack on Tumbleton. Rhaenyra also makes the drastic decision of relieving Mysaria of her duties as master of whispers and banishing her from King’s Landing. This comes after the the two shared an intimate moment in previous episode. As Ormund Hightower and Daemon Targaryen prepare for the battle of Tumbleton, brothers Aegon and Aemon reunite at Harrenhal to discuss plans on how they will take back the Iron Throne. Watch on Deadline Even after delivering imprisoned Sea Serpent, Daemon denies peace talks from Gwayne Hightower setting the stage for the siege of Tumbleton, living up to the hype for which fans have waited weeks. The bloody battle not only leaves the city in ruins but also sees fiery end to Hightower ironically at the hands of Ulf the White and his dragon, who in the previous episode he had persuaded to cross lines and fight for his side. Ulf ultimately turns on both sides burning the city to the ground as Daemon is force to flee. Back in King’s Landing, Rhaenyra comes to find that her prisoner Helaena has taken her own life but left a parting gift for the queen that foreshadows a potential prophecy of Rhaenyra’s path towards madness. When it came to mapping out not just this season, but Season 4 as well, co-creator and showrunner Ryan Condal said he and the writers mapped out a “superstructure” that gave them an idea of how the series would end, and once that came together plotting the rest of Season 3 was seamless. “We were lucky enough in the breaking of Season 3 because we knew at that point that for sure it was going to be a four-season show that essentially when Sarah [Hess] and I sat down with all the writers, we essentially broke the back of seasons 3 and 4 together, at least in the sort of superstructure of it,” Condal said. “So it was really planning out kind of from here to the end and trying to structure it in a way that had all the peaks and valleys of drama and to keep the pacing and to hit all the big set pieces that we have to hit. Once we kind of laid it all out, it felt like it would be really fun to bookend the season with the two biggest sequences we had ever done. So episode 1, Battle of the Gullet, episode 8, the Battle of Tumbleton.” Rhaenyra makes several decisions in this week’s episode that are establishing a path of no return for the upcoming final season. and it’s hard not to see a similar trajectory to another famous Westeros character whose dark choices led to a tragic end. Emma D’Arcy, who plays Rhaenyra, understands how fans could see parallels between Rhaenra and Daenerys Targaryen from the original Game of Thrones and believes their paths has a lot to do with what the Iron Throne represents for all that seek it. “I think the parallels do call to the greater themes of, of the song of ice and fire universe, which is pride and power and how power corrupts and how far it corrupts — it can change good people into corrupted people,” D’Arcy said. “It can take corrupted people and make them real villains. And other people like this era, it can simply just destroy them.” As for the anticipated battle of Tumbleton, Condal says he drew comparisons to when “the Nazis invaded Paris” while ultimately wanting something that looked and felt like a traditional medieval siege. “So all season long, we’re kind of setting up this, this classic medieval siege, which is really where we wanted to get to,” Condall says. “The concept of that battle was that Ormand had basically done all he could to blunt the threat of Rhaenyra’s greatest power, which is that she has, or had, six dragons under her command at that point. He sees his army as better trained and better suited than the river men that are coming to attack. He knows the ground, he’s inside the city. They have to come over the walls, sacrifice a bunch of their men. So that’s where we all started, and then it was like, ‘OK, well, we need to set to do this in a big location, to build it on, and who are POV characters?’ It was a very, very, very complex thing to fold all together, but we just wanted to do the classic medieval siege. [That was] the elevator pitch for the finale.” With the fourth season also marking the final season of House of the Dragon , Condal says while he saw Game of Thrones as an epic story, he always viewed House of the Dragon as more of tragedy. While he won’t say much about what’s to come, he does hint that the final season will be even bigger then the one we just watched Sunday. “We have we have an incredible season coming, as crazy and big as Season 3 was,” Condal said. “I think Season 4 is going to be even bigger. It’s a great privilege to be able to tell a story and to be able to write the ending and to control when and where that ending happens. This is not a given in making television, certainly. So we’re very excited to get back in and we have new characters and new dragons and new locations that I think are gonna make it a very worthy final season.” Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Third Best 2nd U.S. Frame With $145M ‘House Of The Dragon’s Ryan Condal And Emma D’Arcy On Season 3 Finale Now Christopher Nolan’s Highest-Grossing Globally With $1.1B A24’s Anthony Bourdain Biopic ‘Tony’ A Top 2026 Limited Opening Read More About: Comments

full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Heated Rivalry’ Casts Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie As Harris & Troy; Season 2 Debut Confirmed For Spring 2027 ‘Stuart Fails’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’ OG Return For WGA Strike Roast In Magic-Themed Episode 3 Where Wizards Seek “Residuals For Eternal Spells” ‘Stuart’ Episode 3: Wil Wheaton, Brian Posehn & John Ross Bowie Talk Wizards, Puppies, Penguins, Fireball Fight, Easter Egg & That Shocking Death View All August 7, 2026 10:00am L-R: Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie Jonny Marlow; Brindi Tremblay; Sabrina Lantos/Crave Meet Heated Rivalry ‘s newest couple: Justice Smith ( I Saw the TV Glow; Now You See Me: Now You Don’t ) and Charlie Gillespie ( One Night Only, Splitsville, Suze ) are joining returning stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie as leads in the upcoming second season of the hugely popular Crave Original series Heated Rivalry , which is confirmed to premiere in spring 2027. Smith and Gillespie will play Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively, the couple at the center of Role Model , the fifth book in Rachel Reid’s bestselling Game Changers series, on which Heated Rivalry is based. Related Stories News What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far News Upcoming Connor Storrie Projects: From ‘April X’ To ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Production on Season 2 of the show, which streams on HBO Max in the U.S. and several other territories, started earlier this week in Canada. Watch on Deadline After Season 1 adapted Book 2, Heated Rivalry , which chronicles the budding romance between rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), while also incorporating elements from Book 1, Game Changer (featuring Scott and Kip), Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney had said that Season 2 will continue Shane and Ilya’s story by tackling Book 6, The Long Game , while also introducing a new couple by taking on Role Model . Troy Barrett is a hockey player on Ilya Rozanov’s team with a history of bullying while Harris Drover is the team’s cheerful social media manager. “Rachel Reid has given us two beautifully layered characters in Harris and Troy who you can’t help but root for,” said executive producers Tierney and Brendan Brady. “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen. Justice and Charlie do exactly that. They immediately connected with the vulnerability and resilience at the core of these characters, bringing an instinctive understanding of who Harris and Troy are.” In Season 1, Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) are bound by ambition, rivalry and a magnetic pull neither of them fully understood. What began as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies evolved into a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery. Like with the casting of Ilya and Shane, Heated Rivalry is going with one American (Smith) and one Canadian (Gillespie) actor for Harris and Troy. Unlike Williams and and Storrie, who were both complete unknowns with a couple of bit parts under their belts when they were cast in Heated Rivalry , Smith and Gillespie are both established actors with movie and TV series regular roles to their names. Smith also had a role in the Jurassic World movie franchise and headlined Netflix’s series The Get Down . Gillespie, currently seen in One Night Only , additionally starred in Netflix’s Julie and the Phantoms and played a high school hockey player in the 2025 film Shattered Ice . Heated Rivalry , which became an instant global phenomenon when Season 1 was released in late 2025, is commissioned by Bell Media’s Crave, with the participation of the Canada Media Fund. Tierney is writer, director, and executive producer. Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson serve as executive producers. Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje are producers, with Reid as consulting producer. Mike Goldbach serves as co-writer on Season 2. The series is produced by Accent Aigu Entertainment in association with Bell Media’s Crave. It is distributed internationally by Sphere Abacus, a Bell Media company, and is available in more than 130 countries.
